abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of first-line bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin (BEP) chemotherapy in Japanese patients with metastatic germ cell tumors (GCTs). Between 1996 and 2006, 88 male patients with metastatic GCTs were treated with first-line BEP at our institution. Of these 88, 47 (16, seminoma; 31, nonseminoma), who did not receive high-dose chemotherapy following BEP because of the normalization of serum tumor markers, were included in this study. The primary site was the testis in 42 patients, retroperitoneum in 3, and mediastinum in 2. The full-dose regimen used for BEP consisted of cisplatin 20 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5, etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5, and bleomycin on days 2, 9 and 16. Therapeutic outcome was assessed according to several clinicopathological parameters. Following 2 to 4 cycles of BEP (median, 4 cycles), alpha-fetoprotein, beta-human chorionic gonadotropin and lactate dehydrogenase were normalized in all 47 patients. Eighteen patients (38.3%) achieved a complete response (CR) after BEP alone, while BEP resulted in a partial response and stable disease in the remaining 23 (48.9%) and 6 (12.8%), respectively. In addition, surgical resection of the residual tumors following BEP was performed in 15 patients, of whom 12 (80.0%) and 3 (20.0%) achieved pathological and surgical CR, respectively. At a median follow-up of 27 months, all patients were alive; however, disease recurrence occurred in 5 (seminoma, 1; nonseminoma, 4), and all these 5 were subsequently treated with high-dose chemotherapy as salvage therapy. In this series, 1-, 3- and 5-year recurrence-free survival rates were 95.0, 91.4 and 79.2%, respectively, and, there was no significant difference in recurrence-free survival between patients with seminoma and those with nonseminoma. These findings suggested that patients with metastatic GCTs, regardless of histological subtype (i.e., seminoma or nonseminoma), who showed favorable response to first-line BEP chemotherapy, could achieve an excellent prognostic outcome.
abstract_ja: 本研究の目的は、転移性胚細胞腫瘍(GCT)の日本人患者に対する一次治療としてのブレオマイシン・エトポシド・シスプラチン(BEP)化学療法の有効性を評価することであった。1996年から2006年の間に、当施設で88例の男性転移性GCT患者が一次BEPで治療された。このうち、BEP後に腫瘍マーカーが正常化したため大量化学療法を受けなかった47例(セミノーマ16例、非セミノーマ31例)を本研究に含めた。原発部位は精巣が42例、後腹膜が3例、縦隔が2例であった。BEPの全量レジメンは、シスプラチン20 mg/m2を1～5日目、エトポシド100 mg/m2を1～5日目、ブレオマイシンを2、9、16日目に投与するものであった。治療効果は複数の臨床病理学的パラメータに基づき評価した。BEPを2～4サイクル(中央値4サイクル)施行後、47例全例でαフェトプロテイン(AFP)、β-hCG、乳酸脱水素酵素が正常化した。BEP単独で18例(38.3%)が完全奏効(CR)を達成し、残りの23例(48.9%)は部分奏効、6例(12.8%)は安定を示した。さらに15例でBEP後の残存腫瘍に対し外科的切除が行われ、そのうち12例(80.0%)が病理学的CR、3例(20.0%)が外科的CRを達成した。中央値27か月の追跡で全例生存していたが、5例(セミノーマ1例、非セミノーマ4例)で再発が生じ、この5例は全例でサルベージとして大量化学療法を受けた。本シリーズでは、1年、3年、5年の無再発生存率はそれぞれ95.0%、91.4%、79.2%であり、セミノーマと非セミノーマの間で無再発生存率に有意差はなかった。これらの知見は、組織型(セミノーマまたは非セミノーマ)にかかわらず、一次BEP化学療法に良好な反応を示した転移性GCT患者は優れた予後が得られうることを示唆する。
